subject: bright star
title: One Star Was Measured to Be Older Than the Universe Itself

scenes.text: One star was measured to be older than the universe.
It's nicknamed Methuselah. It's 190 light-years away, racing past us at 800,000 miles an hour.
The universe is 13.8 billion years old. In 2000, this star's age came out at 16 billion.
In 2013 Hubble pinned down its distance. New age: 14.46 billion. Still too old.
The escape hatch is the error bar: plus or minus 800 million years. Just enough.
It has almost no iron, so it formed before most stars existed. The latest estimate is 12 billion years.

description:
One star was measured to be older than the universe.
HD 140283, nicknamed the Methuselah star, lies about 190 light-years away in the constellation Libra and moves at about 800,000 mph. In 2000 its age was estimated at 16 billion years; in 2013 a team led by Howard Bond used Hubble to refine its distance and got 14.46 billion years, plus or minus 800 million, against a universe that is 13.8 billion years old. The error bar removes the conflict, and a 2021 study put the star at about 12 billion years. It contains about 1/250th of the Sun's iron, a sign that it formed before heavy elements were common.
What is the oldest thing you have ever seen? Comment below.
first_comment: You can't see Methuselah with the naked eye; it takes a telescope. What space puzzle should we solve next?
